source_text_analysis.full_text: שָׁבוּעוֹת הוּא רְפוּאָה לְהָרֵאָה, כִּי חֲמִשָּׁה כַּנְפֵי רֵאָה כְּנֶגֶד חֲמִשָּׁה חֻמְשֵׁי תוֹרָה (תיקון כה), וּבְשָׁבוּעוֹת מְקַבְּלִין הַתּוֹרָה, יְכוֹלִין לְקַבֵּל חִיּוּת חָדָשׁ
source_text_analysis.translation: Shavuot is a healing for the lung, because the five lobes of the lung correspond to the five books of the Torah (Tikun 25), and on Shavuot we receive the Torah, [so] we can receive new vitality.
source_text_analysis.explanation: The source text uses 'כְּנֶגֶד' (corresponding to / parallel to), which describes a structural numerical correspondence (5 lobes = 5 books). This is not the standard bechina identity formula ('X הוּא בְחִינַת Y' — X is an aspect of Y). The teaching's logical structure is eitza (cause-effect): because Shavuot is when we receive the Torah, and the Torah's five books parallel the five lung lobes, receiving the Torah on Shavuot brings healing to the lung and the ability to receive new vitality. The entire Torah is a single eitza chain. No bechina pairs were identified.

If future enrichment is done on this Torah, this pair should be considered. The source from Tikunei Zohar (תיקון כה) grounds this as a shared-nature claim, not merely a coincidence of number.
